result.topic_en: Dedekind computes the least common denominator of the rational numbers r/a, s/b via gcd/lcm notation and asks whether one can choose an exponent c' coprime to c such that gamma^{c'} = alpha^{rc'} beta^{b_1}, determining the number of such residue classes c' mod c.
result.transcription:
$\left[\frac{r}{a}, \frac{s}{b}, 1\right] = \frac{1}{c}$ $\Big|$ $\frac{r}{a} = \frac{r'}{c}$, $\frac{s}{b} = \frac{s'}{c}$, $1 = \frac{c}{c}$
$[r', s', c] = 1$
$[a, r] = a_1$ ; $[b, s] = b_1$
$\left[1, \frac{r}{a}\right] = \frac{a_1}{a} = \frac{1}{a_2}$ ; $\left[1, \frac{s}{b}\right] = \frac{b_1}{b} = \frac{1}{b_2}$
$\left[\frac{1}{c}\right] = \left[\frac{1}{a_2}, \frac{1}{b_2}\right] = \frac{1}{a_2 b_2}[a_2, b_2] = \frac{\partial}{a_2 b_2}$
$c$ das kl.-gem. Multipl. von $a_2, b_2$
$\gamma = \alpha^r \beta^s$ ; $\gamma^x = \alpha^{rx}\beta^{sx}$ ; $\gamma^c = 1$
Kann man eine relative Primzahl $c'$ zu $c$ so wählen,
dass $\gamma^{c'} = \alpha^{rc'}\beta^{sc'} = \alpha^{rc'}\beta^{b_1}$ wird ?
$sc' \equiv b_1 \pmod{b}$ ; $\frac{s}{b_1} c' \equiv 1 \pmod{b_2}$
Da $[b, s] = b_1$, also $\left[b_2, \frac{s}{b_1}\right] = 1$, so ist hierdurch
$c' \pmod{b_2}$ vollst. bestimmt : $c' \equiv c'_0 \pmod{b_2}$
Da nun $c = \frac{a_2 b_2}{\partial} = \frac{a_2}{\partial}\cdot b_2$, so giebt es immer
$\frac{\varphi(c)}{\varphi(b_2)}$ Classen $c' \pmod{c}$

methods.what: Bringing r/a, s/b, 1 to a common denominator c with coprime numerators
Reduced denominators a_2, b_2 via gcd
c is the lcm of a_2, b_2: gcd of 1/a_2, 1/b_2 equals gcd(a_2,b_2)/(a_2 b_2)
Order of gamma = alpha^r beta^s divides c
Reduction of the condition to a linear congruence mod b_2
Uniqueness of solution mod b_2 by coprimality
methods.quote:
Da $[b, s] = b_1$, also $\left[b_2, \frac{s}{b_1}\right] = 1$, so ist hierdurch
$c' \pmod{b_2}$ vollst. bestimmt : $c' \equiv c'_0 \pmod{b_2}$

methods.what: Counting the admissible classes c' mod c as phi(c)/phi(b_2)
methods.quote:
Da nun $c = \frac{a_2 b_2}{\partial} = \frac{a_2}{\partial}\cdot b_2$, so giebt es immer
$\frac{\varphi(c)}{\varphi(b_2)}$ Classen $c' \pmod{c}$

items.english: Can one choose a number c' relatively prime to c such that gamma^{c'} = alpha^{rc'} beta^{sc'} = alpha^{rc'} beta^{b_1}?
so there are always phi(c)/phi(b_2) classes c' (mod c).
